title: Deterministic kernel ranking, graceful fallbacks, and canary protocol for selection oscillation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: After a scheduler heuristic change rolled 2025-02-10 we observed increased kernel-selection churn across mid-to-large batch workloads which correlated with a 20-40% p95 latency increase on memory-bound attention models. The failure mode manifests as frequent oscillation between two compatible kernels (quantized vs fused-attn heuristic) for similar requests, triggering repeated KV-cache evictions, cache-warmup spikes, and downstream autoscaler/backpressure thrashing. This ticket tracks the investigation, fixes, and rollout plan to stabilize kernel ranking and provide deterministic graceful fallbacks and canary deployment protocols.

Impact: Multiple customers on Dedicated saw elevated tail latency and increased token cost for steady workloads over a 36 hour window before automated rollback. This produced an internal incident and raised SRE Pager alerts tied to autoscaler oscillations.

Scope: Engine runtime scheduler and kernel selection logic, telemetry/metrics, canary gating in the control plane, and synthetic benchmarks to validate fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel-selection churn reduced to <1% for production traffic slices that previously experienced oscillation
End-to-end p95 latency for affected model families returns to baseline within 5% under synthetic and canary traffic
KV-cache miss rate attributable to selection changes reduced by 90% in canary region
Automatic fallback path guarantees no cache-evicting recompile within 30s of a route change
Canary rollout protocol defined and executed with automated rollback on regression signals
action_items: 1) Implement deterministic kernel-ranking comparator: replace floating metric thresholds with stable ordering + smoothing window (owner: Liam) - estimate 3
2) Add selection hysteresis / quiesce window to prevent repeated re-ranking within X seconds (owner: Infrastructure Team) - estimate 2
3) Implement non-evicting fallback path for temporary incompatibility (owner: Runtime) - estimate 3
4) Build telemetry: selection-change counter, correlation tags (model, quant, seq_len, hardware), and an alert when churn > 2% over 15m (owner: Observability) - estimate 2
5) Create synthetic benchmark harness to reproduce oscillation with deterministic seed and high-fidelity KV-cache emulation (owner: Eng Tools) - estimate 2
6) Define canary protocol: percentage ramps, gating metrics (p95, churn, kv-miss), and automated rollback thresholds (owner: SRE/Product) - estimate 1
7) Run 48h canary in a low-traffic region and collect metrics; if stable, roll to broader population (owner: Release Engineering) - estimate 1
8) Post-deploy audit and retro: cost delta analysis and customer communication template (owner: PM) - estimate 1

notes: Root cause hypothesis: selection heuristic used raw score which could flip due to microsecond-level measurement jitter and recent success smoothing at short windows; when two kernels are near-equal the scheduler would flip-flop, creating a feedback loop with cache warming.

Trade-offs discussed: increasing hysteresis reduces responsiveness to genuine performance regressions for long-tail workloads. Deterministic ranking + smoothing offers better balance than purely increasing thresholds.

Mitigation timeline: short-term feature-flagged comparator + canary (2 weeks), medium-term guardrails in autoscaler and cache policy (1 quarter), long-term: model-centric profiling to label kernel compatibility buckets (future work).
